RUST DEPENDENCY LICENSES AND COPYRIGHT NOTICES

Scope: exact registry packages in engine/Cargo.lock. This is intentionally a
superset of Windows release dependencies: development, build-time, optional
bundled components and other platform packages are included too. Inclusion does
not assert that every package is linked into the Windows binary. The project
native engine is licensed separately under engine/LICENSE (release copy:
ENGINE-LICENSE.txt).

Every complete .crate archive was verified against its Cargo.lock SHA-256 before
reading notices. Source URLs and checksums identify exact provenance. All located
license alternatives and copyright/authorship notices are reproduced below.
For r-efi this distribution uses the MIT option, whose full grant and copyright
holders are in AUTHORS; that file also describes unselected alternatives.
The two winapi GNU-target import-library archives omit standalone licenses but
retain their original copyright and references to the workspace MIT/Apache terms.
Their own notices are included, supplemented with the full license files from
the same upstream project's Cargo.lock-pinned winapi 0.3.9 archive; those separate
source URLs and checksums are labelled explicitly. Bundled SQLite/SQLCipher
opening notices are also labelled and retain complete source-file checksums.
No build-machine paths, account data or inferred author names are added.

--- sqlite3/sqlite3.c [opening copyright/license notice] ---
Original source-file SHA-256: c01235302fe80da901fb70c7622c39147e29d9f29b7f6eb746b23517f320c90d

/******************************************************************************
** This file is an amalgamation of many separate C source files from SQLite
** version 3.46.0.  By combining all the individual C code files into this
** single large file, the entire code can be compiled as a single translation
** unit.  This allows many compilers to do optimizations that would not be
** possible if the files were compiled separately.  Performance improvements
** of 5% or more are commonly seen when SQLite is compiled as a single
** translation unit.
**
** This file is all you need to compile SQLite.  To use SQLite in other
** programs, you need this file and the "sqlite3.h" header file that defines
** the programming interface to the SQLite library.  (If you do not have
** the "sqlite3.h" header file at hand, you will find a copy embedded within
** the text of this file.  Search for "Begin file sqlite3.h" to find the start
** of the embedded sqlite3.h header file.) Additional code files may be needed
** if you want a wrapper to interface SQLite with your choice of programming
** language. The code for the "sqlite3" command-line shell is also in a
** separate file. This file contains only code for the core SQLite library.
**
** The content in this amalgamation comes from Fossil check-in
** 96c92aba00c8375bc32fafcdf12429c58bd8.
*/
